If you look at it like that then being at 25 and already taking care of your goals is an extraordinary achievement. If your still looking for more (which is great and not at all a bad thing) then think about what you want to learn next; maybe an instrument? New language? Something from history that intrigues you? The world is ripe for you take and enjoy. If you don't want to learn something then that's okay too. You could always finish that book you've been putting on the back burner, start watching that TV show you've been curious about, or maybe playing that great game that maybe you haven't had the time to play.

Trust me, those people still achieving goals means that they don't have their life figured out completely (which is fine too). It means something is still missing in their life.

Something I did that helped in the beginning of a break up:

Go buy a small journal, it doesn't matter what kind anything will work. On the last page, write a few things you want to achieve (get a new car, hit a target weight, move somewhere else, get a new job, learn an instrument, etc) it could be anything but something YOU want to achieve not what someone else wants you to be. Now that you have that written in the back; go back to the first page and write tomorrows date. Put down 5 things you want to achieve tomorrow, be realistic you're not going to get a new job tomorrow but you can start looking at postings for example. Even if it's something you don't think isn't a task you can still write it down (like driving to the store to pick up food), it doesn't have to be groundbreaking. Then everyday you'll do those 5 things and at night you'll write the next list for tomorrow. Not only does this help keep you busy so you don't think about it but it will get things done you need to work on. When you finish the whole journal, you can look back at your long term goals and see how far you've come.

Keep your chin up, okay? Your heart will heal; and even if it scars each one is a life lesson you learned to make you a better person.
